restrictions: Target sha256-r31-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..30 on every padded block, standard IV used once, FIPS 180-4 padding, full feed-forward, all eight digest words. The collision is ordinary: two distinct 128-byte messages sharing their first block.

The scored program is a deterministic replay of one stored, organizer-verified colliding pair (proof.md Section 3). It uses no random coins, so success_probability is exactly 1 for the fixed target. It is not a generator and claims no amortised cost.

The stored pair is the colliding pair published by Li, Liu, Wang, Dong and Sun (ASIACRYPT 2024). Its whole one-time construction is specified step by step in proof.md Section 7 and charged once as preprocessing inside total time (proof.md Section 8). That includes trail search, starting solutions, the lookup table, first-block matching, completion and checking.

Ledger total 2^40.75317 target-compression units: the published two-phase total 2^40.5, per-trial word operations 2^34.44, trail-search allowance 2^38, set enumerations 2^27.11, the check, and the 6.36-unit replay. Claimed 40.76 leaves about 2^33.0 units of slack.

One score-critical heuristic, H1, covers the published 2^40.5 figure and the 2^38 trail-search allowance. Collision correctness, distinctness and success probability do not depend on it. Two supporting heuristics are also declared: H2 for the memory metric and H3 for the C3 acceptance cross-check. Neither changes time_log2.
Memory is a reported metric only. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.

heuristics.statement: The one-time construction of the stored pair (proof.md Section 7, steps C0-C5) costs at most L1+L2+L3+L4+L5 of proof.md Section 8, which is 2^40.75317 target-compression units. (a) Starting solutions, table, first-block matching and completion (C1-C4) cost at most the 2^40.5 compressions that the source authors report for this trail, start and step count; per-trial word operations are added separately as L2. (b) The characteristic search C0 costs at most 2^38 units.
heuristics.scope: The ASIACRYPT 2024 31-step SHA-256 trail of proof.md Section 5, standard IV, steps 0..30, and the one-time construction of one colliding pair. It says nothing about other step counts, trails or prefixes, and nothing about repeated or amortised generation.
heuristics.extrapolation: (a) The source states time 2^40.5 and memory 2^19.8, and a practical run of 1.2 hours on 64 threads, which is 2^22.42 compressions per thread-second. Its framework total includes the solver time per starting solution, and a public re-run of a comparable solve suggests about 2^35.9 units for 54 starting points. We reproduced exactly the C2 record of the stored pair, the enumerated V5/V6 set sizes (whose product 2^-27 is the C3 acceptance probability under H3) and every predicate of C1-C5 on the pair. (b) A public re-run of the authors' four-stage trail search took 16,580.78 CPU-seconds, which is 2^36.60 units at 2^22.58 units per CPU-second or 2^36.44 at the source rate. The allowance 2^38 is 2.6x to 2.9x that and above a 6-IPC, 5.5 GHz hardware ceiling (2^37.90).
heuristics.limitations: The 2^40.5 figure is the authors' analysis plus one practical run, not an organizer-model trace, and we did not reproduce the per-match completion rate inside it. The trail-search bound rests on a re-run of the public tool, not on the authors' original logs. Sensitivity: the claim fails if L1+L3 exceeds 2^40.5+2^38 by more than about 8.8e9 units. A trail search costing 2^39 would give 2^40.95, and a C1-C4 cost of 2^41 would give 2^41.19.

heuristics.statement: The peak resident memory of the one-time construction (C0-C5) is at most 2^32 bytes. Solver calls in C0/C1 run one at a time, as specified in proof.md Section 7, and each needs at most the 2.13 GiB peak measured in a public re-run of the same open-source tool. The C2 table (2^25.8 bytes) and the bucket index (2^22 bytes) add to that.
heuristics.scope: This construction, executed sequentially as specified. It says nothing about parallel executions; running k solver calls concurrently would multiply the solver term by k. It affects only the reported memory metric, not time_log2, success or correctness.
heuristics.extrapolation: The 2.13 GiB peak comes from one public re-run of the authors' tool (credited in proof.md Section 12) on this trail. The table and index sizes follow directly from the record counts in Section 7.
heuristics.limitations: We did not re-run the solver ourselves. If one call peaked above about 3.9 GiB, the bound would need 2^33. That would change only the reported memory.

heuristics.statement: In step C3, after key matching, the words W5 and W6 behave as jointly uniform and independent over their admissible ranges. The per-candidate acceptance probability is then the product of the enumerated set fractions |V5|/2^32 and |V6|/2^32, which is 2^-27.
heuristics.scope: Used only as an internal consistency check of the published two-phase total L1. The score charges L1 as published (under H1); it does not recompute L1 from this probability. Collision correctness and replay success do not depend on H3.
heuristics.extrapolation: The set sizes |V5| and |V6| were computed exactly by exhaustive enumeration over 2^32 words each (proof.md Section 6). Joint uniformity and independence after matching are assumed, not proved: W5 and W6 are computed from different message words through the step function, and the matching constraint fixes other words.
heuristics.limitations: If W5 and W6 were correlated, the true acceptance rate could differ from 2^-27. The published 2^40.5 total, which the authors obtained in a practical run, would still be the charged figure under H1. The only effect would be on how well this cross-check supports H1.
